paper_title: MMAR A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio,   Music, and Their Mix
caption: : Task Taxonomy
model_annotation: The chart presents a task taxonomy for the MMAR benchmark, comprising 20 categories of analysis. The categories are grouped into three layers: Signal Layer (4.3%), Cultural Layer (14.1%), and Semantic Layer (41.2%), with the largest remaining portion labeled as Perception Layer (40.4%). The Signal Layer includes Anomaly Detection, Acoustic Quality Analysis, Audio Difference Analysis, and Signal Layer. The Cultural Layer comprises Imagination, Culture of Speaker, Asthetic Analysis, Professional Knowl & Reasoning, and Spatial Analysis. The Perception Layer contains Counting & Statistics, Music Theory, Correlation Analysis, Temporal Analysis, and Environmental Perception & Reasoning. The Semantic Layer consists of Speaker Analysis, Emotion & Intention, and Content Analysis. Notably, the chart features a legend, with percentage labels provided for the three layers and some inner categories. The segments are visually arranged in a descending order of size, with the Perception Layer occupying the largest area, followed by the Semantic Layer, and then the Cultural and Signal Layers.
